turns.thought:
I was able to find your account, John. Let me check a few account-level things first before we dig into the phone itself.

I've confirmed:
- Your line **555-123-2002** (line ID L1002) is **Active** — not suspended
- Your device (Smartphone Pro Max, ID D1002) shows as **activated**
- Your data usage is **8.7 GB of 15 GB** — well within your limit, so that isn't the cause
- Your most recent bill (B1002, $150.00) isn't in overdue status, so billing isn't blocking your service

Since everything looks good on the account side, this is most likely a setting or hardware issue on the phone itself. Let's work through some checks together.

**Step 1: Check your status bar**

Look at the very top of your phone's screen. Could you please use the **check_status_bar** option on your device and tell me exactly what icons it shows? Specifically I'm looking for:
- Any airplane mode icon (✈️)
- Signal strength (📵 No Signal, 📶¹ Poor, 📶² Fair, etc.)
- Mobile data status (📱 Data Enabled or 📵 Data Disabled)

Just read me whatever it lists and we'll go from there. Take your time — there's no rush.

Great find — that's almost certainly the culprit! Airplane Mode turns off all of your phone's wireless radios (cellular, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth), which is exactly why you're seeing "No Service" and can't use data.

The good news is this is a very easy fix.

**Step 2: Turn Airplane Mode OFF**

Please use the **toggle_airplane_mode** option on your device to switch Airplane Mode **OFF**. (If you'd rather do it manually: swipe down from the top of your screen to open Quick Settings, find the airplane icon, and tap it so it's no longer highlighted. Some phones also have it under Settings → Network & Internet → Airplane Mode.)

**Step 3: Wait a moment, then re-check**

After you turn it off, give your phone about 30–60 seconds to reconnect to the network, then run **check_status_bar** again and let me know what it shows.

Now you should hopefully see:
- No more ✈️ icon
- A signal strength reading, like 📶³ Good
- A network type, like 5G or 4G

Go ahead and try it, and tell me what the status bar says afterward. If the signal comes back, we're all set. If it still shows "No Signal" or "No Service," we'll keep troubleshooting — a loose SIM card or a network setting would be the next things to look at.

Good progress — the airplane icon is gone, which confirms that fix worked. But you're still showing "No Signal," so there's something else going on. Don't worry, we have several more things to check.

I also notice it says **📵 Data Disabled** — that's a separate issue we'll come back to. But right now, no signal is the priority, because mobile data can't work until the cellular connection is restored.

**Step 4: Check your SIM card**

The SIM card is the small chip inside your phone that identifies you to the network. If it's loose, has shifted slightly, or isn't being read properly, you'll get exactly this symptom — no signal even though everything else is fine.

Could you please run **check_sim_status** on your device and tell me what it reports?

It will come back with one of these:
- **"Active"** — the SIM is fine, and we'll move on to other checks
- **"Missing"** — the phone can't detect the SIM at all (very fixable)
- **"Locked"** — there's a PIN/PUK security issue (I'd need to get additional help for that one)

I'll also mention: I can see from your account that your SIM was last replaced on **January 20, 2025**, so it's relatively new.

Go ahead and check that for me and let me know what it says.

I understand why that's concerning, but let me reassure you on a couple of points.

**What this means:** A SIM PIN is a short security code (usually 4-8 digits) that can be set to lock the SIM card itself. Many phones ship with a default PIN set by the carrier, or one may have been set when your SIM was replaced in January. It's a security feature designed to prevent someone else from using your SIM if the phone is lost or stolen — so it's actually protecting you, not a malfunction.

**Why it caused your problem:** When the SIM is locked, it cannot register on the network. That's exactly why you have no signal and no service despite Airplane Mode being off.

**Here's where I have to hand you off.** SIM PIN/PUK security is handled by our dedicated technical support team for your account's protection — I'm not able to unlock it or provide PIN/PUK codes from my side, and I'd strongly advise against guessing at codes on your end. Entering the wrong PIN too many times will permanently lock the SIM, and at that point the only fix is a full SIM replacement. So let's get you to someone who can verify your identity and walk you through it safely.

Let me transfer you now.
